central.finding: There are two central routes. The TD School runs Transdisciplinary Electives, a suite of 8 undergraduate electives, each built around a challenge co-designed with a named partner over three years. UTS Shopfront brokers community-organisation projects into coursework, where student teams act as consultants. The TD School also runs the Industry Innovation Project, a final-year partner project in the Bachelor of Creative Intelligence and Innovation (BCII).

schemes.module_code: e.g. 95002/95010 TD: Reframing, remixing, reimagining society (UNICEF Australia); 95005 Shaping Technologies that Shape Us (Microsoft); 95004 (ServiceRocket); 95006 (City of Sydney); 95008 (Miro); Pathways to Societal Transitions (Lane Cove Council)
schemes.description: A suite of 8 TD School elective subjects open to UTS undergraduates. Each subject is built around a real-world challenge from a partner organisation (2026 partners include UNICEF Australia, City of Sydney, Microsoft, Miro, Lane Cove Council and ServiceRocket). Partners co-design a challenge or learning question that runs for three years, contribute pre-recorded learning modules, and join live sessions (Q&As, mentoring, feedback on student ideas). Students from across faculties develop proposals in response; in a 2024 offering, Red Cross students pitched proposals to Australian Red Cross staff (search summary).
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: All UTS undergraduate degrees with elective space; BCII students take different electives
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: Undergraduates with elective space; BCII students excluded (they take their own elective subjects).
schemes.credit_assessment: 6 cp (e.g. 95002) or 8 cp '+' version (e.g. 95010) per 2026 handbook / 2027 pre-approved list. Group assessment format for 2026 not verified; the pre-2025 handbook for 95009 lists a 40% major task with a 10-minute presentation, poster and Miro board.
schemes.duration: One teaching session (e.g. 95002 fortnightly in Autumn, or July block)
schemes.delivery_format: Fortnightly in session or block mode; mix of pre-recorded partner content and live sessions
schemes.project_evidence: Each subject centres on a real-world challenge presented by an industry partner, and students develop projects and ideas in response [1][2][3]. Outputs in past offerings were proposals pitched to the partner (Red Cross, 2024) and presentation/poster/Miro board deliverables (95009, pre-2025) [4].
schemes.group_evidence: Student page (fetched): "Collaborate in teams with students from all faculties across UTS"; "all about teamwork and real-world projects" [6]. Team assessment format in the 2026 handbook not verified.
schemes.employer_evidence: Partner organisations co-design the challenge/learning question for three years, contribute pre-recorded learning modules, and take part in live engagements: Q&As, mentoring, and feedback on student ideas [2][3]. Every subject has a named partner (one 2026 listing showed TBC) [3].
schemes.partner_role: Sets the challenge, provides content, mentors and gives feedback; receives pitches in some offerings
schemes.named_partners: 2026: UNICEF Australia, City of Sydney, Microsoft, Miro, Lane Cove Council, ServiceRocket [3]; earlier: Australian Red Cross, Stockland, Regen Studios (search summary)
schemes.deliverable: Team proposals/ideas responding to the partner challenge (presentation, poster, Miro board in a pre-2025 example)
schemes.unresolved: Whether assessment is a group output was not verified in 2026 handbook; the student page states teams. Page says "eight electives are embedded in every undergraduate degree" (availability, treated as optional elective). Delivery rests on dated 2026 brochure and 2026 handbook entry.

schemes.description: Final-year project subject in the Bachelor of Creative Intelligence and Innovation (BCII). The subject coordinator allocates students to multidisciplinary teams of 5–7 based on core degree and preferences. Each team works for 13 weeks on a partner-organisation brief. Students present a reframed brief to the partner, agree a plan, hold weekly check-ins with a partner mentor, and give a final presentation of initiatives, insights and prototypes with a report.
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: Bachelor of Creative Intelligence and Innovation (combined with students' core degrees)
schemes.credit_assessment: Final presentation and report (weighting not retrieved)
schemes.delivery_format: In-session team project with weekly partner check-ins
schemes.project_evidence: Partner brief, which students reframe; final presentation of initiatives, insights and prototypes with a report [1][2].
schemes.group_evidence: Coordinator allocates students into multidisciplinary teams of 5–7 [1] (search-summary paraphrase of partner page).
schemes.employer_evidence: Partners must assign a dedicated mentor or main contact. The mentor attends weekly check-ins, a midpoint check-in and the final presentation; the partner gives feedback on the reframed brief and receives the final solution. Partner time commitment is 25–30 hours [1][2].
schemes.partner_role: Supplies brief, mentors, gives feedback, receives final presentation
schemes.unresolved: Not confirmed whether the subject is a core BCII requirement. Partners described only as 'industry partners', so sector mix is unverified. Projects are chosen by student vote from partner proposals.

schemes.official_name: UTS Shopfront Community Program – community projects in coursework
schemes.description: Pro bono brokerage. Not-for-profit organisations and social enterprises submit projects they need. UTS students take them on in coursework subjects, working in teams as external consultants for credit, usually in final year or at postgraduate level. Each organisation nominates a contact who gives up to 2 hours per week. Projects run in the Autumn (March–June) or Spring (August–November) session. Past projects include research for the HIV/AIDS Legal Centre (NSW).

profile_md:
**UTS (reduced-depth, all six areas queried).** Qualifying or near-qualifying routes were found centrally and in one faculty.

**TD Electives** (TD School, 8 subjects, 6-8cp): the student page states each elective has "a real-world challenge presented by an industry partner organisation" and "Collaborate in teams with students from all faculties"; partners (UNICEF Australia, City of Sydney, Microsoft, Miro, Lane Cove Council, ServiceRocket in 2026) co-design the challenge, mentor and give feedback. Optional, open to undergraduates except BCII students.

**Industry Innovation Project** (BCII final year): 13-week teams of 5-7 with partner mentors. **UTS Shopfront** brokers charity/community projects into coursework as team consultancies, but host subjects are unidentified.

**Software Development Studio** (FEIT): teams of 4-6 deliver prototypes for industry-posed briefs over 12 weeks with weekly industry mentors; optional, listed FEIT degrees; page undated (copyright 2026) so current delivery unconfirmed.

**Strategic Communication capstone**: semester-long real-client brief; team format not stated.

Business, engineering capstone, design and science instances were seen only as titles or snippets. Provision is distributed across several routes; no compulsory institution-wide route found.
gaps: Business School capstones, engineering/IT capstones, Mechanical and Mechatronic Design studio, Strategic Design Studio: not verified beyond snippets; further departmental instances likely. Shopfront host subjects and Industry Innovation Project core status unresolved. SDS and Strategic Communication lack dated delivery evidence. Law and health: no live-client team subject surfaced (one combined search only). 2026 handbook assessment for TD Electives not retrieved.
